title.en: Past continuous: I was walking when it started
title.sl: Past continuous: kaj se je ravno dogajalo (I was walking)
title.de: Das past continuous: was gerade los war (I was walking)
title.it: Il past continuous: che cosa stava succedendo (I was walking)

rule.sl:
*past continuous* pove, kaj se je ravno dogajalo v nekem trenutku v preteklosti: **was** (I, he, she, it) ali **were** (you, we, they) + glagol z **-ing**: **I was walking.** (Ravno sem hodil{m:|f:a}.) **We were working.** (Ravno smo delali.) Slovenščina to pove z nedovršnim glagolom in z besedo *ravno*.

Zanikanje: **wasn't**, **weren't**: **It wasn't raining.** (Ni deževalo.) Za vprašanje gre was ali were na začetek: **Were you sleeping?** (Si ravno spal{m:|f:a}?) **What were you doing?** (Kaj si ravno delal{m:|f:a}?) Kratki odgovor: **Yes, I was.** **No, I wasn't.** Nikoli *Did you sleeping?*

Glavna raba: nekaj dolgega je trajalo, **when** (ko) se je zgodilo nekaj kratkega. Dolgo z -ing, kratko v *past simple*: **I was walking when it started to rain.** (Ravno sem hodil{m:|f:a}, ko je začelo deževati.)

**while** (medtem ko) gre z dolgim: **While I was cooking, the phone rang.** Dve dolgi dejanji hkrati: **While Jack was shearing, Meg was sleeping.** (Medtem ko je Jack strigel, je Meg spala.)

Zgodba se pogosto začne tako: **It was raining and the wind was blowing. Suddenly the door opened.** (Deževalo je in pihal je veter. Nenadoma so se odprla vrata.)

Pravopis je kot v sedanjiku: **making**, **sitting**, **lying**. Glagoli za stanja nimajo -ing: **I knew the way.** Nikoli *I was knowing the way*.
rule.de:
Das *past continuous* sagt, was in einem Moment der Vergangenheit gerade los war: **was** (I, he, she, it) oder **were** (you, we, they) + Verb mit **-ing**: **I was walking.** (Ich ging gerade.) **We were working.** (Wir arbeiteten gerade.) Das Deutsche hat dafür keine eigene Form, höchstens *gerade*.

Verneinung: **wasn't**, **weren't**: **It wasn't raining.** (Es regnete nicht.) In der Frage kommt was oder were nach vorn: **Were you sleeping?** (Hast du gerade geschlafen?) **What were you doing?** (Was hast du gerade gemacht?) Die Kurzantwort: **Yes, I was.** **No, I wasn't.** Nie *Did you sleeping?*

Das Wichtigste: Etwas Langes war im Gang, **when** (als) etwas Kurzes passierte. Das Lange mit -ing, das Kurze im *past simple*: **I was walking when it started to rain.** (Ich ging gerade, als es zu regnen begann.)

**while** (während) steht beim Langen: **While I was cooking, the phone rang.** Zwei lange Dinge zugleich: **While Jack was shearing, Meg was sleeping.** (Während Jack schor, schlief Meg.)

So beginnt oft eine Geschichte: **It was raining and the wind was blowing. Suddenly the door opened.** (Es regnete, und der Wind blies. Plötzlich ging die Tür auf.)

Die Schreibung ist wie im Präsens: **making**, **sitting**, **lying**. Verben für Zustände bekommen kein -ing: **I knew the way.** Nie *I was knowing the way*.
rule.it:
Il *past continuous* dice che cosa stava succedendo in un momento del passato: **was** (I, he, she, it) o **were** (you, we, they) + il verbo in **-ing**: **I was walking.** (Stavo camminando.) **We were working.** (Stavamo lavorando.) Somiglia a stare + gerundio al passato, e spesso all'imperfetto.

Negazione: **wasn't**, **weren't**: **It wasn't raining.** (Non pioveva.) Per chiedere, was o were va all'inizio: **Were you sleeping?** (Stavi dormendo?) **What were you doing?** (Che cosa stavi facendo?) La risposta breve: **Yes, I was.** **No, I wasn't.** Mai *Did you sleeping?*

L'uso principale: un fatto lungo era in corso **when** (quando) è successo un fatto breve. Il lungo in -ing, il breve al *past simple*: **I was walking when it started to rain.** (Stavo camminando quando ha cominciato a piovere.)

**while** (mentre) va con il fatto lungo: **While I was cooking, the phone rang.** Due fatti lunghi insieme: **While Jack was shearing, Meg was sleeping.** (Mentre Jack tosava, Meg dormiva.)

Spesso una storia comincia così: **It was raining and the wind was blowing. Suddenly the door opened.** (Pioveva e soffiava il vento. All'improvviso la porta si è aperta.)

L'ortografia è come al presente: **making**, **sitting**, **lying**. I verbi di stato non prendono -ing: **I knew the way.** Mai *I was knowing the way*.
rule.en:
The past continuous says what was going on at a moment in the past: **was** (I, he, she, it) or **were** (you, we, they) + the verb with **-ing**: **I was walking.** **We were working.**

No: **wasn't**, **weren't**: **It wasn't raining.** To ask, was or were goes first: **Were you sleeping?** **What were you doing?** The short answer: **Yes, I was.** **No, I wasn't.** Never *Did you sleeping?*

Its main use: something long was going on **when** something short happened. The long one with -ing, the short one in the past simple: **I was walking when it started to rain.**

**while** goes with the long one: **While I was cooking, the phone rang.** Two long things at once: **While Jack was shearing, Meg was sleeping.**

A story often opens with it: **It was raining and the wind was blowing. Suddenly the door opened.**

The spelling is as in the present: **making**, **sitting**, **lying**. Verbs for states take no -ing: **I knew the way.** Never *I was knowing the way*.
